characters: Pokuaa: a fourteen-year-old JHS 3 sewing-group leader wearing a tape measure around her neck, precise and level-headed.
Seyram: her classmate designing a QR-code digital product catalogue on a school tablet.
Abdul-Aziz: their classmate and enterprise bookkeeper, quick with probability and percentages.
Miss Tetteh: the JHS Computing teacher supervising the school’s digital enterprise club.

narrationPlan.voice: Confident, alert teen voices for Pokuaa, Seyram, and Abdul-Aziz; smooth, deceptive caller voice contrasted with calm Computing teacher Miss Tetteh
narrationPlan.pace: Alert, sharp, and practical (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.
Pronounce spreadsheet formulas, geometric terms, and security acronyms clearly and unhurriedly.

music: Crisp kora-style acoustic plucking with subtle modern digital pulse resolving cleanly (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Proposed NaCCA CCP curriculum links: Computing (B8.1.1.1 QR Codes, B8.3.3.1 Information Security—CIA Triad), Career Technology (B8.2.1 Textiles, B8.6.2 Enterprise), and Mathematics (B8.4.2.1 Probability, B8.1.3.1 Percentages & Discounts).
Ghana Cyber Security Authority (CSA) Relevance: Directly addresses Mobile Money social-engineering OTP scams and fake reversal messages targeting youth enterprises.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?
Are all mathematical calculations, Career Technology safety rules, and Computing syntax 100% accurate?
Verify exact NaCCA Information Security terminology: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability.
Check discount and fee arithmetic: 5% of GH¢ 200 = GH¢ 10 (net GH¢ 190); 1% of GH¢ 590 = GH¢ 5.90; probability = 1/10,000.

teacherGuide.overview: Links Career Technology textile craft and enterprise bookkeeping with NaCCA Computing Information Security (CIA triad, QR codes, phishing defence) and BECE Probability & Commercial Percentages.
learningGoals: Explain the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) and recognise phishing traps.
Protect PINs and 6-digit OTPs from social-engineering attacks.
Calculate simple probabilities for PIN guessing and compute trade discounts and fees.

beforeReading: Write two URLs on the board: https://example.com and http://example.invalid/free-bonus—ask students to spot warning signs.
whileReading: Pause on Page 3 to match real examples to CIA Triad pillars.
afterReading: Calculate how much fabric is needed to sew a laptop sleeve when seam allowance is added to every side.
discussion: Why do scammers always try to create panic ("within two minutes!") during phone attacks?
reflection: Without revealing your real PIN, check silently: is any password you use based on a birthday or 1234?

mathsExtension.task: A padlock uses 3 dials, each numbered 0 to 9. How many total combinations exist, and what is the probability of opening it on one random guess?

support: Use a physical 3-column chart matching CIA Triad pillars to everyday school scenarios.
stretch: Explain how Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) combines something you know with something you have.
